_about: The Ideas tab of This Week's Publish Board (wC 19 Oct): the ideas Krish picks from, one per day. Each fact was checked on 18 Oct 2026 against the source linked beside it; a company's own claim is labelled as one. No titles here: titles, headlines and thumbnail words are Krish's, after he records (TITLES_AFTER_RECORDING). Built into the board by scripts/post-pack/week_board.py --ideas.

mon.from: Engine's Sunday research (already on the week page)
mon.story: Google's newest model is on a teaser rate: follow one price from Google's bill to the buyer's bill to what a business selling AI work can safely charge once it doubles.
mon.why_now: Gemini 4 Argon went generally available on 13 October 2026; the launch price ends on 30 November.
mon.fact: $2 in and $10 out per million tokens until 30 November 2026, then $4 and $20 from 1 December; cached input goes from $0.10 to $0.20 the same day.

source.label: eesel.ai, Gemini 4 Argon pricing (Google's own pricing page to be read at the fact gate)

mon.from: Your Instagram inspo (@therundownai saved it) and the 14 Oct ideas research
mon.story: When an AI app millions of people loved goes bust, who walks away with the money? Google paid billions for the people; Disney is bidding millions for what is left; the users get nothing.
mon.why_now: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware on 12 October 2026; objections are due 23 October and the bidding hearing is 30 October.
mon.fact: Disney is the lead bidder at $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual licence to Character.AI's technology; in August 2024 Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license its models.

mon.story: Who pays for a free AI picture: you, or the brand in the progress bar? ChatGPT starts showing ads while your image draws, and only to people who do not pay.
mon.why_now: OpenAI announced the test on 5 October 2026; it starts in the US later in October.
mon.fact: A sponsored banner appears below the progress bar while an image renders, for free users only; paid subscribers stay ad-free, and DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science police where ads may appear.

mon.from: Your Instagram inspo (saved) and the 14 Oct ideas research
mon.story: Nvidia's biggest customer is building its way out: Microsoft will run most of its own AI on its own chip, so who keeps the margin, and does anyone's AI bill go down?
mon.why_now: Microsoft announced Maia 300 on 12 October 2026; it becomes the main system behind Microsoft's own products from 2027.
mon.fact: Microsoft says Maia 300 gets 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems (its own estimate, not independently checked).

wed.from: Your words, 14 and 17 Oct ("deep dive into grok versus Muse bots for medium businesses and do a bake-off"; "Add Viktor")
wed.story: The bake-off: Grok Bot, Muse and Viktor, with OpenClaw as where it started, put to work for a business of 50 to 1,000 people, rated separately on what each is useful for and what each could break.
wed.why_now: Your ask for this week; Grok Bot's public LEGO order (11 to 13 Oct) shows what goes wrong when an assistant spends for you.
wed.fact: Musk told Grok to find and order LEGO Star Wars kits; his own screenshot showed his order number, his email and the last four digits of his card, and a stranger then said he got LEGO's support bot to cancel it.

wed.from: Your words, 17 Oct ("what happens when you just keep adding all of your tools and connectors into your AI tools")
wed.story: Plug Gmail and Drive into your AI and what does it really get: what it can read, what it keeps, what it learns from, and whether the convenience is worth what the company gets.
wed.why_now: Your ask on 17 October; Meta and Sierra's agent standard (6 Oct) is built around what agents may see and do for you.
wed.fact: ChatGPT may keep an indexed copy of what it syncs from a connected Google app, deleted within 30 days of disconnecting; OpenAI says that data does not train its general models, but Memory may use it.

source.label: Knightli summary of OpenAI's data-controls FAQ, 20 Jun 2026 (OpenAI's own page to be read at the fact gate)

wed.from: 14 Oct ideas research (radar), sequel to last Wednesday's Muse piece
wed.story: Take apart the new rulebook for AI shoppers that Meta and Walmart signed and Amazon did not, and see whether it fixes what Amazon said was wrong with Muse.
wed.why_now: Announced 6 October 2026; the first draft followed that week.
wed.fact: Sierra's Bret Taylor announced the Personal Agent Protocol with Meta, Walmart and Stripe; Amazon, which blocked Meta's Muse from shopping on its site, is not a partner, and Anthropic is not named.

wed.from: Your Instagram inspo (saved) and the 14 Oct ideas research
wed.story: Apple's first home AI screen, taken apart before it ships: what recognising your face actually unlocks, what is still in beta, and why Europe cannot buy it.
wed.fact: HomeView is $299 in the US, recognises up to six people in a household, and is not sold in the EU at launch because Siri AI is not available there.

fri.from: Engine's Sunday research (already on the week page)
fri.story: The people who check the labs from outside depend on insiders who work for the lab; when OpenAI fired three of its safety staff, one says over how he talked to the outside checkers, the gap showed.
fri.why_now: OpenAI fired the three on 9 October 2026.
fri.fact: OpenAI fired Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni citing broken rules on sensitive information; Korbak says he was told it was over how he communicated with METR; OpenAI says it was not about safety concerns.

fri.from: Your cold idea in the Inspo folder, 9 Oct ("unpacking models by country")
fri.story: Where an AI was built is starting to decide what it says no to: ask Claude, then a Chinese model, the same thing, and the answers split by where the model was built.
fri.why_now: The @evolving.ai post you saved (about 11 Oct); the piece runs its own dated side-by-side test before it says anything.
fri.fact: In a Christian Science Monitor test of 200 prompts, Chinese-owned chatbots refused, repeated government lines or got it wrong about a third of the time, DeepSeek nearly two times in three (reported second hand; the original to be read at the fact gate).

source.label: Let's Data Science, on the Monitor's September 2026 test

fri.from: Your Instagram inspo (the Danish bill was saved) and the 14 Oct ideas research
fri.story: As AI makes copying anyone free, owning a face, a voice or a character is becoming the part that keeps its value: Denmark, Disney and Character.AI in the same fortnight.
fri.why_now: Denmark's bill was introduced on 8 October 2026; Disney's bid for Character.AI's licence followed on 12 October.
fri.fact: Denmark's bill L 49 would make it unlawful to publish a realistic AI imitation of someone's face, voice or movements without consent, with the publisher having to prove consent; it is meant to apply from 1 January 2027 if passed.

fri.from: Engine's Sunday research (already on the week page)
fri.story: A video call no longer proves there is a person on the other end, and most companies using video agents have not written down when they will say so.
fri.why_now: Tavus showed Griffin on 1 October 2026, three weeks before Friday.
fri.fact: In Tavus's own one-minute test, 26 of 54 people took Griffin-Lite for a human, against 1 of 41 for its previous system; they had been told they would talk to another participant.

fri.story: AI is moving out of data centres into the cheap boxes in our homes; Anthropic's own test shows how far that has got, and how far it has not.
fri.why_now: Anthropic's red team published on 12 October 2026.
fri.fact: Anthropic ran a large open model across 15 Android TV boxes costing about $55 each, slowly; no model reliably copied itself onto the real TV it was tested on, and the move to smaller models is the team's estimate.
